ranking.verdict: The most screenshot-able idea in the set: a swaying original printed into a bent toner copy, with cause and effect on one line and a 'copy the copy' loop that degrades to a black silhouette; it is print material in the Ink/Halftone vein, has four presets, and had no open issues.
ranking.tryFirst: Press Enter five times and watch the generations collapse into toner.
ranking.risk: No second review pass and not checked in a browser. For about 900ms the canvas fades over an offset static card, so a ghosted double card shows; the Copy button and thumbnails look disabled during the first pass. Lifting a copy does a synchronous 5MB readPixels, which may hitch.

ranking.verdict: Ebru marbling made from real album covers that can be un-pulled exactly is beautiful and easy to remember, and its presets panel matches the Ink exemplar; the second polish now pulls the comb through the hero cover on load (confirmed in code: introPull/rushIntroComb).
ranking.tryFirst: Pick Comb, drag across the album, then drag back to un-pull it.
ranking.risk: The intro comb pull (about 96px of tooth travel) and the larger stone windows have not been seen on screen. Rebuilding the bake on resize or preset change is a one-off cost. Without Spotify the sheet is marbled from baseball-card scans.

ranking.verdict: The most satisfying piece in the first five seconds: rub a cover into a coloured dune, then watch about 15k grains erupt and land as the next album; the strata re-homing (strataHomes, drift) is in the code.
ranking.tryFirst: Rub half the cover loose, then press the right arrow.
ranking.risk: The strata bands were only simulated headlessly and may still read as pixel-sorted streaks. The bottom 30% of the tray is mostly empty at load. Without Spotify the fallback covers are trading cards.

ranking.verdict: A believable booking card whose signature line really behaves like wet ink, with beads, coffee rings and a blotter offprint; it is the strongest interface-first piece and fits Herb's 'interfaces, not abstractions' taste, and the black-flash bug is fixed (the governor now runs before paint).
ranking.tryFirst: Sign your name, hold the pen still at the end, then Sign and book.
ranking.risk: The new glint strength and longer wet time are untuned and could read as outlines on thin strokes. The ghost lift of the intro autograph has not been seen. The fallbacks (RGBA8, Canvas2D) are much plainer.

ranking.verdict: Pulling a letter out of a giant song title until its strands neck and snap, pop pop, is instantly tactile and memorable; the near-miss hit test that changed the title is fixed in code (rowBoxes, two-radius grab).
ranking.tryFirst: Grab the y in the title and pull it down hard.
ranking.risk: Glyph rasterisation still runs on the main thread when a title changes. The hand-lag and lurch feel was only checked in a Node sim. Key-driven grabs do not have the lag.

ranking.verdict: A clean, efficient piece that demonstrates itself (a lens sharpens a cover down to pixels while flat areas stay chunky) and morphs into the next album's tree from your click; it had no open issues, but the idea is less striking than the five above.
ranking.tryFirst: Move the cursor slowly across a face, then click another cover.
ranking.risk: The root pop is mostly hidden by the 900ms canvas fade, and there is a faint light-then-dark flicker at the handoff from the placeholder. Without Spotify it shows card scans.

ranking.verdict: An album cover as woven cloth whose rows you fling into shear waves that pluck a pentatonic strum: rich, physical and musical; the Linen retune (tension 120, coupling 4800) is in the code, so the wave now reaches the whole cloth.
ranking.tryFirst: Grab a middle row and fling it sideways.
ranking.risk: The landing damping and the column-by-column weave sweep have not been seen on screen. Audio needs a first gesture. A second fling while the cloth is still ringing travels less far.

ranking.verdict: A Calder mobile of covers that rebalances when you tap one up to the top, with weight and consequence in the Deck/Flyout spirit; the idle-forever rAF loop is gone and beat-driven bobbing was added.
ranking.tryFirst: Tap the smallest bottom cover and watch the mobile rebalance.
ranking.risk: The jukebox half (preview, hum, beat bob) needs Spotify credentials; on this machine it hangs card scans and the player shows as a caption only. The beat thresholds were tuned on a synthetic kick, not real audio.

ranking.verdict: Iron filings that engrave the cover and comb into field lines around draggable magnets are beautiful and calming; the opening now runs on simulation time (simTime/advanceOpening confirmed) and gained a travelling ripple, but it is less of an instant wow than the pieces above.
ranking.tryFirst: Tap the magnet to flip it and watch the ripple sweep.
ranking.risk: The ripple costs about 0.37ms per turning magnet at 8.8k filings, which may be heavy on phones. Without WebGL2 the Canvas2D fallback draws half the filings. Card-scan covers without Spotify.

ranking.verdict: Tearing a perforated ticket off a roll, bridge by inked bridge, is a satisfying physical gesture on a real-feeling object; the tease now leaves four torn bridges and slow pulls snap back, which earns it the last place in the batch.
ranking.tryFirst: Twist the end ticket from its corner until it tears off.
ranking.risk: The tease tear angle relies on the reviewer's sim, and the snap-back spring keeps a small overshoot. The preview on tear needs Spotify. A forced rebuild resets a part-torn seam.

ranking.verdict: Font weight as fluid dye in a wall of song titles is a clever, very 'herb.art' idea, but it is more abstract than the batch, and whether the whorl keeps visibly spinning (the MacCormack fix is in the code) is still unproven on screen.
ranking.tryFirst: Whip a fast loop through the middle of the wall.
ranking.risk: The spiral arms may still merge into a blob. The CPU fluid plus MacCormack cost is estimated, not measured. A late font load re-assembles the wall once.

ranking.verdict: Diving through the hole of a letter into the next song is memorable, but the porthole is small at rest (20 to 80px) and the wheel and trackpad input model is complex and was fragile in review, so it sits just outside the batch.
ranking.tryFirst: Two-finger swipe down on the trackpad to fall through songs.
ranking.risk: The momentum-tail heuristics and wheel notch handling were rewritten and not tested in a browser. Up to 24 porthole masks (about 0.7MB each) stay in memory.

ranking.verdict: A cover cut into sampler pads that play beats of the real song is a great instrument, but it depends on preview audio, and on this machine the songs are paired with baseball-card art, so the first impression is weaker.
ranking.tryFirst: Tap a pad, then tap three others over it.
ranking.risk: Every sound depends on the iTunes preview lookup. Covers whose lookup fails are hidden. Without Spotify the fallback titles do not match the card art. Beat slicing on real previews is untested in a browser.

ranking.verdict: A convincing datamosh with motion-vector arrows; it reads as a codec and not a blur, but it is closer to an abstract effect than an interface and was the lowest first-round score.
ranking.tryFirst: Drag hard across the cover, then tap to keyframe.
ranking.risk: Tick legibility at the vote frame and the seam between the CSS cover and the canvas crop are unverified. CORS cache reuse of the SSR image is assumed.

ranking.verdict: Song titles at the type scale as harp strings with sympathetic resonance is witty and musical, but the visual is quieter than the others and the wow needs sound.
ranking.tryFirst: Drag down through all the lines, then pull the biggest one.
ranking.risk: The CSS-to-canvas entrance handoff uses bezier fits and is not bit-exact. Font strings are still rebuilt per frame on lines that ring while resizing. The iPhone audioSession fix is untested.

ranking.verdict: Burning ink like a fuse is a strong idea, but it had the most review issues (four), its intro bite and fire tuning were checked only in a CPU port, and fire on album art edges toward a spectacle demo.
ranking.tryFirst: Hold still on dark lettering until it lights.
ranking.risk: The intro bite on real covers is unseen and can be smothered by introLimit if it touches ink. Choosing the Fuse preset early leaves the intro unable to light. Card-scan covers without Spotify.

ranking.verdict: Darkroom developer sloshing over a print is atmospheric, but the default John source is 200px and soft at 7x enlargement, and the press-well fix that makes the liquid follow your finger is untested.
ranking.tryFirst: Press and hold on the face and drag slowly.
ranking.risk: The default print is still soft (only sharpened). PRESS_DEPTH may feel greedy and drain the rest of the sheet. Shader compile now uses async status polling.

ranking.verdict: A tab bar whose indicator is one thread that unstitches and restitches icons is lovely craft, but it is a small, subtle detail rather than a wow.
ranking.tryFirst: Drag from Home across to Profile and let go.
ranking.risk: The join between the canvas strand and the SVG dashoffset was traced by hand only. iTunes covers are cached for an hour.

ranking.verdict: An Up Next queue on an elastic thread is a tidy product component, but the wave still risks reading as 'list slides up plus a twitch', and it is the least memorable of the twenty.
ranking.tryFirst: Swipe the third song off hard to the right.
ranking.risk: Downstream rows sway only about 5 to 8px. Now uses iTunes art; the last-resort fallback falls back to monogram beads.

ranking.verdict: Scratching a printed spectrogram with the lyrics on it could be great, but it is the only piece that lost score (6), and it depends entirely on one audio clip and its timing offset.
ranking.tryFirst: Grab the tape mid-phrase and yank it backwards.
ranking.risk: Local audio files are missing here, so it relies on the iTunes preview at a measured 25.6s offset. If Herb's local clip differs, the words will be mis-timed. The lyrics lane needs the Spotify env.
